items.title: Public Meeting re Proposed Amendment to the Community Improvement
notes: Plan

items.title: Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of the public meeting is to present
notes: and receive public input regarding a proposed update to the Township Urban Centre Community Improvement Plan prior to making a decision.

He noted the Township has recently completed a review, finishing the preparation of an updated CIP, referenced as the 2023-CIP. The 2023- CIP provides financial incentive programs for properties within Township boundaries.

He indicated if a person or public body does not make oral submissions at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the update is adopted, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT).

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submission at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the update is passed, the person or public body may not be added as the party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters advised if anyone wishes to be notified of the adoption of the proposed update to the CIP, a written request must be filed with the Municipal Clerk, Township of Centre Wellington, 1 MacDonald Square, Elora, ON N0B 1S0.

The Municipal Clerk advised notice was mailed to prescribed persons, agencies and public bodies on or before October 19, 2023. A copy was published in the Wellington Advertiser on October 19, 2023 and October 26, 2023. She confirmed the requirement for giving notice was completed on October 19, 2023.
Sally Litchfield, Economic Development Coordinator provided an overview of the CIP update and introduced the consultant, Luciano Piccioni, President, RCI Consulting.

Luciano Piccioni provided a project update and outlined the community improvement project area, the incentive programs, the implementation and administration process, the monitoring and marketing plans, and the final steps, including notice of adoption and the 20 day appeal period.
There being no registered delegations, Mayor Watters provided an opportunity for Members of Council to ask questions.
L. Piccioni responded to questions regarding any current applications and the evaluation process for the incentive programs.
Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and advised Council will be considering the matter later on in the meeting.
Mayor Watters declared the meeting adjourned.

items.title: Battery Energy Storage Systems - Request for Municipal Support
notes: Resolutions
Report from S. Litchfield, Economic Development Coordinator Delegations

Dave Anders, Alectra Energy Solutions and Trevor Tempson, Convergent provided an overview of the Belwood Energy Storage project and a request for a municipal support resolution. D. Anders provided background on the joint venture between Alectra and Convergent. He indicated the Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are safe, affordable, long-lasting energy resources that will make Ontario’s electricity grid cleaner, more reliable and more resilient. He noted the project and community benefits, indicating the Alectra Convergent joint venture recognizes the importance of partnership with the Township and is offering a meaningful long-term investment in the community.

The representatives responded to questions regarding community outreach conducted to date, the connection to Hydro One as a transmission interconnection and the importance to protect agricultural lands.

Ondrej Benjik, Director of Development, Aypa Power provided an overview of Aypa, details regarding the Elora Battery Energy Storage System, feedback from community engagement held and shared visual concept renderings of the Elora project and community endorsements.
He responded to a question regarding studies associated with the impact on agricultural lands.
Council recessed and returned at 8:30 pm.

S. Litchfield, Economic Development Coordinator provided an overview of the report, indicating staff is of the opinion battery energy storage system facilities should be located on employment land and not in prime agricultural area.

Mayor Watters noted staff has suggested two recommendations for Council consideration. Councillor Wilton suggested a third option to split Option 1 and consider the requests of Aypa and Alectra separately.
Discussion ensued and staff responded to questions.

motions.item_title: Report from the Committee of the Whole – November 14, 2023
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve the report from the Committee of the Whole dated November 14, 2023 as follows. 1. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receive for information the presentation by Watson and Associates with respect to the Centre Wellington Land Needs Review. 2. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receive for information a report on the Province of Ontario's proposed changes to the Clean Water Act regulations and streamlining various approvals for low risk construction activities. 3. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington adopts a Township-initiated Official Plan Amendment to designate certain lands Core Greenlands and Residential to implement County Official Plan Amendment No. 69 to expand the Urban Growth Centre boundary and facilitate development of certain lands; THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington recommends to the County of Wellington that proposed draft plan of subdivision 23T- 18002, as modified, be granted draft approval, subject to the conditions of approval set out in Schedule "A" to staff report PLN2023-46; and THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves rezoning application RZ06/18 and that the appropriate zoning by-law amendment be given three readings. 4. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves a single source contract award for the engineering design, installation and commissioning of an odour control system for the Clyde Street Wastewater Pumping Station to Environmental & Power Solutions Inc. at an upset limit of $383,007 including non-rebate HST, as outlined in Report No. IS2023-30. AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves an additional $1,500.00 including non-rebate HST from the Wastewater Capital Reserve to fund the anticipated project overage. 5. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve the inclusion of the 10-Year Capital Forecast as outlined in report COR2023-104 dated November 14, 2023 in the Draft 2024 Budget. 6. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve the inclusion of the 2024 Draft Budget Debt Requirements and Capacity as outlined in report COR2023-105 dated November 14, 2023 in the Draft 2024 Budget.
